findings.title: The second downsize definition replaces the existing API
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods by argument count: this definition replaces the downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) method immediately above it. Existing calls with width, height, and options now raise ArgumentError; calls with just width and height bind the height to opts and fail when optimize indexes it as a hash. Keep a single method that explicitly supports both calling conventions, or give the dimensions-string variant a different name.

findings.title: Downsizing multipart GIF uploads discards their animation
findings.body: The resize operation receives the multipart tempfile path rather than a path carrying the original filename's extension. Such paths normally have no .gif suffix, but OptimizedImage.optimize selects its animation-preserving implementation only when the input path ends in .GIF. Consequently, even with allow_animated_thumbnails enabled, an oversized animated GIF goes through convert with the [0] frame selector. Because the output overwrites the upload itself, the stored original permanently loses every frame except the first. Determine the image format independently of the tempfile suffix and preserve animation when downsizing the original.

findings.title: Keep the configured size limit for attachments
findings.body: The hard-coded 10 MB limit applies to attachments as well as images, although the new server-side downsizing only handles images. Attachments larger than max_attachment_size_kb now pass client validation and are uploaded before being rejected by the server. Conversely, sites configured to allow attachments larger than 10 MB can no longer upload them through this client. Retain the configured attachment limit and apply any larger pre-downsizing limit only to images.
